name: Liberation theology
summary: Liberation theology is a Christian movement that began among Latin American Catholic theologians in the 1960s and reads the Gospel from the standpoint of the poor and oppressed. It holds that God has a preferential option for the poor, that sin has a social and structural dimension, and that salvation includes historical liberation from poverty and injustice, using social analysis that draws on Marxist concepts. It organises through grassroots base communities and has been criticised by the Vatican for politicising the faith.
scope: Mainstream Latin American Catholic liberation theology of the 1960s to 1980s, based on Gustavo Gutiérrez (A Theology of Liberation, 1971), Leonardo Boff, Jon Sobrino, Archbishop Romero and the Medellín conference of 1968. It excludes Protestant, Black, feminist, Dalit, Palestinian and other strands except where noted, and the Vatican's own positions except as a reference point. Most answers are inferred because the movement rarely addresses statements outside theology, economics and violence.

keyFigures.name: Gustavo Gutiérrez
keyFigures.role: Peruvian priest who coined the term and wrote A Theology of Liberation (1971).

keyFigures.name: Leonardo Boff
keyFigures.role: Brazilian theologian and leading exponent, silenced by the Vatican in 1985.

keyFigures.name: Óscar Romero
keyFigures.role: Archbishop of San Salvador who became a symbol of resistance to military repression.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Archbishop Romero and Gutiérrez gave priority to non-violence and reform, though some, such as Hélder Câmara, did not condemn armed resistance.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Inferred from the critique of hierarchy and of a privileged class; the Church hierarchy was called part of a privileged class.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Liberation theologians reread history from the standpoint of the poor and oppressed rather than a national or civilizational centre; inferred, not a stated curriculum position.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: The movement grew out of a critique of dependency and domination by richer powers, and treats paternalist rule over the poor as part of the structural sin it opposes.

patriotic-education.rationale: Inferred from the movement's solidarity with the poor across borders and suspicion of state-serving ideology; it is not a stated position.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Inferred from the preferential option for marginalized groups, which favours measures that widen opportunity for the excluded.

public-money-creation.rationale: Not addressed directly; inferred from its call for public and communal control of economic life over private accumulation.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Its Marxist-influenced social analysis treats capitalism as structurally unjust, though the movement does not rest on a collapse prediction; inferred.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Inferred from its opposition to neocolonial domination, which makes cultivating influence over former dependencies unattractive.

delink-world-market.rationale: Dependency theory shaped the movement, and many theologians argued the poor of the periphery are kept poor by integration into the world capitalist system.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: Its analysis centres on oppression of the poor of the Third World, but it speaks of the poor and the oppressed in common rather than splitting workers; inferred.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Inferred from the defence of the dignity of every person and the option for the poor, which opposes discrimination against anyone.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Romero and the bishops defended human rights against state repression, so written guarantees fit the movement; entrenchment itself is inferred.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Inferred from dependency analysis of colonial legacies; not stated for treaties.

elective-rulers.rationale: Inferred: the 1986 Instruction affirms democracy and participation, which the movement shares.

minority-veto.rationale: Inferred: the movement favours majority participation and rejects a single-member veto.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Romero called on soldiers to refuse orders to kill and defended resistance to unjust rule.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Inferred: solidarity and love for the poor imply duties for the rich, though the movement stresses structural change over paternalism.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Faith is held to demand political commitment on the side of the poor.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Inferred: the movement uses Marxist-influenced social analysis of ideology and class.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Inferred: Marxist-influenced analysis of ideology and institutions.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Dependency theory, central to the movement, holds poverty results from the structure of the world economy.

native-born-offices.rationale: Inferred: preferential option for the poor implies equal rights, not birth-based offices.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Dependency theory suggests delinking, but the movement also seeks international solidarity; split.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Inferred: Romero and the movement stress peace and human rights.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Inferred: the movement centres the oppressed, including indigenous peoples.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Inferred: Romero opposed military dictatorship and repression.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Inferred: the movement rejects equating communism and fascism, and treats Marxism as an analytic tool.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: Inferred: mainstream account taken as given.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Not addressed by the movement; inferred indifference, so adherents are treated as split.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Not addressed by the movement; inferred indifference, so adherents are treated as split.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Inculturation is valued but the movement also claims universal human rights; split.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Romero denounced military repression and the army role in killings.

paid-care-work.rationale: Not addressed by the movement; inferred indifference, so adherents are treated as split.

filial-duty.rationale: Inferred: the movement stays within Catholic social teaching on family, which affirms obligations to parents.

office-by-exam.rationale: Inferred from its stress on popular participation and base communities over technocratic or elite selection.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Inferred from its critique of economic dependency of poor countries on foreign capital.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Inferred: the movement stays within Catholic teaching on marriage and its indissolubility.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Inferred from base communities and grassroots participation, which favour accountability of leaders to the people.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Inferred from its solidarity ethic, which favours collective provision over individualised private savings.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Inferred from its support for land reform and the Catholic idea that goods are meant for all.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Inferred from its support for democratic institutions against military dictatorships in Latin America.

single-official-language.rationale: Inferred from its defence of the culture and rights of indigenous and poor communities.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Inferred from its critique of dependency and its support for land going to local peasants.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Inferred from its focus on structural sin and structural causes of injustice rather than individual intent.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Inferred from its critique of capitalist accumulation and its call for simplicity alongside the poor.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Inferred: Romero and most mainstream figures criticised violence, though some strands justified revolutionary force; foreign arming was not their cause.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Inferred from its opposition to imperial domination of Latin America and its stress on the autonomy of peoples.

corporate-influence.rationale: Inferred from the critique of structural sin and economic dependency, which targets concentrated wealth shaping institutions.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Inferred: the movement itself relied on foreign church funding and solidarity, though its dependency critique is wary of foreign capital.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Not addressed; the Church backs families but the movement centres on poverty and justice rather than population policy.

residents-only-property.rationale: Not addressed; the movement favours land reform for the poor but has no stance on residency limits for buyers.

job-guarantee.rationale: Inferred from the preferential option for the poor and the right of all to dignified work, which the Vatican framework also affirms.

democratic-peace.rationale: Not addressed; adherents distrusted Western-style democracy promotion while valuing human rights and democratic participation.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Adherents are split: Romero urged soldiers to disobey unjust orders, but the Church framework holds that legitimate authority binds in conscience.

non-intervention.rationale: Inferred as split: the movement opposed US intervention in Latin America yet supported international solidarity and human-rights pressure against atrocities.

industrial-unions.rationale: Inferred from support for organised labour and mass popular organisation of the poor; the movement has no stated view on craft versus industry.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: The Gospel-based ethic of the movement and the Church reject scapegoating of minorities, and it locates oppression in structures, not hidden plots.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Catholic theologians treat marriage as a sacrament and the movement did not challenge its legal recognition.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Inferred from the movement's stress on truth-telling, human rights and exposing state repression, as in Romero's denunciations.

local-production.rationale: Inferred from the dependency critique and support for peasant and community economies, in base communities.

informal-organisation.rationale: Base communities are small grassroots groups central to the movement, though it still works within the institutional Church.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Inferred: the movement appealed to international human-rights standards against repressive national governments.

religious-nation.rationale: Inferred: the movement defines the people by the poor and oppressed, not by shared creed, and works for ecumenical solidarity.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the critique of dependency on rich powers and the call for justice among nations.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the preferential option for the poor, which favours sharing resources toward the needy.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Not addressed directly; inferred from the movement's turn toward socialism, which targets productive property rather than personal belongings.

defeat-communism.rationale: The movement rejected anticommunist crusading and drew on Marxist analysis, though it did not endorse communist states.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from a preference for public provision that serves the poor over profit-driven providers.

religion-illusion.rationale: Adherents are Christian believers who reject the Marxist view of religion as illusion, a point the Vatican instruction itself stresses.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: The movement saw Latin American poverty as produced by capitalist dependency and structural sin, not as a foundation for better things.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Not addressed by the mainstream Latin American strand; inferred from its view that structural injustice must be changed, not only attitudes.

socialized-care.rationale: Not addressed; adherents are not clearly split but the movement has no stated position on public domestic services.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from its concern for the poor and indigenous peoples rather than language purity.

treaties-binding.rationale: Not addressed directly; inferred from solidarity with indigenous and oppressed peoples and their claims to justice.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Inferred from the grassroots base communities, though these are church communities rather than a model for all of society.

majority-settlement.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from its stress on equal dignity and the rights of the poor and oppressed.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Gutierrez favoured socialism while the Vatican warned against Marxist analysis, and adherents differ over whether this is a third way.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Indigenous land struggles get support but the theology has no stance on historic or religious land claims; strands differ (for example Palestinian).

holocaust-denial.rationale: Inferred from its concern for victims of oppression and Church condemnation of antisemitism.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from Catholic teaching against criminalisation and the focus on the oppressed.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Romero denounced repression and defended people's rights to organise against the regimes of El Salvador.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Its call is freedom and liberation of the poor, with respect for conscience; inferred as opposed to state punishment of belief.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Liberation theology grew out of dependency theory, which treats rich countries' domination of the periphery as structural injustice.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: Not addressed; Latin American theologians had no interest in jihad, inferred against.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Resistance to unjust rulers is justified by the poor's liberation and rights, not by their lack of religious law.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Base ecclesial communities and the poor as agents of their own liberation are central to the movement.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Poverty, race and gender oppression are treated together in later strands; the mainstream emphasis is class and poverty, so inferred.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from Catholic teaching on sex and gender.

assisted-dying.rationale: Catholic teaching on the sanctity of life is retained by mainstream Latin American liberation theologians.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from its clear partisan option for the poor.

alienated-labor.rationale: Liberation theologians used Marxist analysis of exploitation, which the 1984 Vatican instruction criticised.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Inferred from its dialogue with indigenous and pluralist Latin American contexts and Church teaching on dialogue with other religions.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Catholic doctrine holds that authority comes from God, mediated by the people; inferred.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from Catholic institutional tradition.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from concern for the vulnerable against powerful employers.

social-market-economy.rationale: It criticises capitalism as structural sin, though it proposed no single model; inferred as rejecting a market economy with welfare.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from its opposition to militarism and Latin American military regimes.

rich-first.rationale: The preferential option for the poor puts the poor first; inferred as opposing letting some grow rich first.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Third-world solidarity and dependency analysis imply keeping out of the great-power blocs; inferred.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Inferred: a movement centred on the poor and on grassroots communities has little room for hereditary rule.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Inferred: credit cooperatives fit the option for the poor, but the movement did not take a position on bank ownership.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Inferred from its critique of structural injustice and the dependency theory it drew on; Latin American debt burdens were criticised.

property-franchise.rationale: The preferential option for the poor rules out limiting political voice to the propertied.

domination-women-nature.rationale: Inferred: later liberation theologians such as Boff linked ecology and women's liberation, though this was not central to the 1970s core.

reification.rationale: Inferred: the movement used Marxist-influenced social analysis of structures of domination, as the Vatican's 1984 Instruction criticised.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Inferred from its critique of structural sin and the power of the wealthy over the poor.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Inferred: Romero and others denounced arbitrary state violence and called for justice under law.

racial-franchise.rationale: Medellin and the movement affirm the equal dignity of all people, so racial limits on citizenship are rejected.

online-participation.rationale: Anachronistic; the movement is indifferent to internet participation.

open-government-data.rationale: Inferred from its demand that the powerful be answerable to the poor.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Inferred: the movement stressed Christian freedom and liberation and showed no support for legal bans on interfaith marriage.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: The commitment to the oppressed and to human dignity rejects targeting a minority's shops.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Inferred from the movement's base communities and stress on poor people's own participation; sortition itself is never discussed.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: The movement rereads scripture and doctrine from the standpoint of the poor and present conditions, which the Vatican instruction criticises as reinterpretation, though it does not reject tradition outright.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: The movement holds that structures of sin and dependency concentrate wealth and power in ways that oppress the poor, and denounces unequal ownership.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Inferred from its commitment to the dignity of the marginalised; the movement rarely addressed it and Church teaching on sexuality limited its stance.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: It is a Christian movement working inside the Church, and the Vatican documents it answers affirm religious freedom, so promoting atheism is contrary to it.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Inferred from its concern for the poor who suffer police and prison abuses, though it mostly criticises abuses of order rather than abolishing the institutions.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: The movement does not address this and adherents are indifferent.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: It stresses structural change and justice over charity, as Libertatis Nuntius notes of its critique of merely charitable responses.

term-limits.rationale: The movement does not address this; adherents are indifferent.

vote-delegation.rationale: Inferred from the base-community model of participatory grassroots decision making; delegation of votes is not discussed.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: Not addressed; adherents are indifferent and the concern is historical liberation of the poor.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Inferred from its liberation of the marginalised; the Vatican position is against women priests, so adherents are split and this is contested.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Inferred from its emphasis on equality and dignity in base communities; marriage authority is not discussed.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Not addressed directly; inferred from the preferential option for the poor and solidarity with the marginalised, including migrants.

rent-control.rationale: Inferred from the priority given to the needs of the poor and the critique of structural injustice in housing and land.

abolish-ip.rationale: Not addressed; adherents focus on poverty and land, and no common position on intellectual property is documented.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Inferred from the movement's emphasis on grassroots base communities and critique of militarised nationalism.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Not addressed directly; inferred from Catholic and Latin American church opposition to nuclear weapons and the movement's concern for the vulnerable.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Inferred from the movement's critique of dependency and of US domination over Latin America.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Inferred from the stress on remembering victims of oppression and state violence, as in Romero's denunciations of killings.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: The preferential option for the poor and the critique of capital accumulation imply that income should reflect labour and need rather than ownership.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Most liberation theologians treated violence as a last resort and a few accepted just resistance to oppression, so absolute pacifism is not the movement's line.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Inferred from the focus on the universal church and the poor across nations rather than on national identity.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Not addressed by the mainstream strand; this scope excludes feminist liberation theology.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Not addressed by the mainstream strand; this scope excludes feminist liberation theology.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Romero and others are honoured as martyrs of faith and justice, but the statement concerns death for the nation, which the movement does not centre.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: The movement reads history as a struggle between justice and structural sin, with the Gospel as the standard, though it grounds this in concrete social analysis.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: Not addressed; the movement is not concerned with diaspora homelands.

culture-before-state.rationale: Inferred from the stress on liberating structural change over purely spiritual or cultural renewal.

god-not-male.rationale: Not addressed in the mainstream strand, which is not focused on gendered language for God.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: Not addressed in the mainstream strand; judging scripture by women's full humanity belongs to feminist theology, outside this scope.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Inferred from the movement's universalism and solidarity with all the poor, including minorities and indigenous peoples.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: Not addressed; no documented position on territorial units for peoples.

independent-unions.rationale: Inferred from the movement's defence of workers' and the poor's organisation and from its criticism of oppressive state power; not addressed directly.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: Inferred from the preferential option for the poor and the call for the poor to be agents of their own liberation, though adherents rarely use this framing.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Inferred from the preferential option for the poor and the critique of structural injustice, which favours public provision of essentials.

second-chamber.rationale: Not addressed by the movement; no position can be inferred.

municipal-property.rationale: Inferred from its critique of private capital and its sympathy for communal and cooperative ownership, though it did not endorse municipal ownership specifically.

confederal-coordination.rationale: Not addressed by the movement; adherents favoured base-community decision-making but did not address confederations.

family-wage.rationale: Catholic social teaching, which Romero and the Vatican instructions both draw on, holds that wages must be enough to support a worker and his family.

faster-drug-approval.rationale: Not addressed by the movement; no position can be inferred.

ageing-research-funding.rationale: Not addressed by the movement; adherents would stress access for the poor over this spending priority.

anonymous-payments.rationale: Not addressed by the movement; adherents prioritised the poor's welfare and were wary of state repression, but no stance can be inferred.

online-anonymity.rationale: Inferred from Romero and base communities needing to speak out safely under military regimes, though the topic is anachronistic.

person-over-state.rationale: The Vatican's 1986 instruction on freedom and liberation and Gutierrez both ground liberation in the dignity of every person, who is never a mere means to a collective end.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Gutierrez and the Vatican instructions state that salvation includes but exceeds historical liberation and that politics must serve the whole human person, spiritual as well as material.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: Not addressed by the movement; adherents split on how national and regional power should be divided.

gm-crops.rationale: Not addressed by the movement; no position can be inferred.

dense-cities.rationale: Not addressed by the movement; no position can be inferred.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Inferred from its universal option for the poor of every race, though Black and indigenous strands treat racial identity differently.

racial-pride.rationale: Not addressed by the mainstream Latin American strand; adherents are split.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Romero and the movement opposed military repression and Medellin condemned violence, but some adherents accepted armed struggle as a last resort, so the camp is split.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the movement's universal solidarity of the poor, which cuts across national and linguistic lines rather than defining nations.

communal-electorates.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the base-community ideal of one people of God and equal citizenship of the poor, not separate confessional blocs.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Not addressed; the movement blames foreign economic dependency and domination, but a partition plot is not part of its analysis.

free-public-college.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the preferential option for the poor and the aim of opening education to them.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Not addressed in the 1960s-80s core texts; inferred from the structural-sin critique that makes the powerful bear the costs they impose on the poor.

future-generations.rationale: Not a core 1960s-80s topic; inferred from the Christian doctrine of stewardship of creation, which Boff later developed.

women-distinct-values.rationale: Not addressed; the movement stresses the poor's perspective, and adherents are split on a distinct women's contribution.

arms-reduction.rationale: Not addressed directly; inferred from Romero's and the movement's opposition to military repression and arms in the service of oppressive regimes.

open-diplomacy.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the movement's critique of powerful states and elites acting without accountability to the poor.

capital-controls.rationale: Inferred from dependency analysis, which blames unequal global capital flows for poverty in Latin America.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: Inferred from the concern for order and protection of the poor against violence; base-community theologians sometimes defended armed resistance, so adherents vary.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Adherents are split: peace and conscience are stressed, but theologians such as Camilo Torres endorsed armed struggle.

collective-bargaining.rationale: The preferential option for the poor supports workers' organisation, and Catholic social teaching has long backed unions.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: Inferred from the preferential option for the poor, which backs public help for low-paid families, though tax credits are not discussed.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Inferred from the critique of debt and austerity burdens on the poor; adherents rarely favour binding rules that limit social spending.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: Liberation theology grew from dependency theory and calls for reordering international economic structures, including debt, in favour of poor nations.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Romero and the mainstream tradition pressed for structural change through church, base communities and politics, mostly not insurrectionary destruction of the state.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: Inferred: adherents favour popular and community economic forms, but the sources set out no pluralist stance on a blueprint.

nature-as-capital.rationale: Inferred from the Gospel view of creation as gift; adherents tend to resist treating nature as priced capital.

sacred-nation.rationale: Inferred: the Gospel stresses a universal community, and the sources treat the nation as secondary to the poor and the church.

student-debt-relief.rationale: Inferred from the preferential option for the poor and concern with the debt burden on the powerless; not a stated position.

internal-colonialism.rationale: Dependency theory behind the movement describes the rich centre exploiting the periphery, extended by adherents to regions within countries.

shared-human-nature.rationale: The Vatican instruction and Gutierrez both ground human dignity in the person made in the image of God.

public-service-media.rationale: Inferred from concern for a voice for the poor and the church's own media; independence from commercial control fits the option for the poor.

religions-one-truth.rationale: Liberation theologians work inside Christian revelation and treat it as the truth, not as one expression of a universal spirituality.

farm-price-support.rationale: Inferred from the preferential option for the poor, which supports protecting small farmers from market and credit exploitation.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Inferred from Catholic social teaching and Romero's pacifist stress on peace and the poor, though nuclear arms were not central to the movement.

workers-own-party.rationale: The movement backed popular and base organisations of the poor, including peasant and labour parties, as part of liberation.

ban-fgm.rationale: Inferred from the stress on human dignity and the liberation of the oppressed; the movement did not address FGM.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: The option for the poor and the dignity of the oppressed imply equal legal rights for women, though gender was a later concern.

one-language-many-names.rationale: The movement never addressed language naming; adherents have no shared view.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: Inferred: structural sin points to strong public remedies for harm to the poor, but individual liability is not discussed; adherents are split.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: Inferred: the movement often defended indigenous communities, but it favoured popular participation over official roles for chiefs.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: Inferred from Romero and later Boff on creation, though the movement focused on the poor; environmental concern grew from the 1980s.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: Inferred from the stress on mercy and structural causes of crime and on the poor, which resists rigid punishment.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: The movement stressed the poor and migrants but never addressed language rules; adherents are split.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: Inferred: the movement sided with organised workers and the poor, so it would back union solidarity over an open-shop rule.

voter-id.rationale: Inferred: its concern is with the poor's full participation in politics, so it would resist barriers that exclude them, though it never addressed voter ID.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: Inferred from the Church's religious-liberty teaching and its support for human rights in its 1986 statement, though adherents are Catholic and treat Catholic doctrine as normative.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: Inferred: it values democracy as participation and justice for the poor, so elections alone without social justice would not suffice.

premarital-sex.rationale: Inferred: adherents remain within Catholic sexual teaching, though some base communities were more flexible.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: Romero and the movement defended human rights against state repression, and censorship of communication would be seen as an instrument of it.

negative-income-tax.rationale: Inferred: the movement sought structural change and solidarity, not replacement of welfare with a market-style cash payment.

women-suffrage.rationale: Inferred from its human-rights language of the equal dignity of all persons, which the Church's 1986 statement stresses.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: Inferred: as Christian believers, adherents hold that religion liberates, though they acknowledge oppression in church and social structures.

race-social-construct.rationale: Inferred from the Christian teaching of the equal dignity of all persons and the movement's solidarity with the oppressed.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: Inferred from its commitment to the equal dignity of women and the oppressed, though it did not address agencies.

homestead-ownership.rationale: Inferred from the preferential option for the poor and the critique of structural injustice in property, which treats private appropriation of land as subordinate to the common good.

international-criminal-courts.rationale: Inferred from Romero's denunciation of state atrocities and the movement's concern for victims of repression; it did not address international courts directly.

scripture-inerrant.rationale: Liberation theologians read scripture historically and from the standpoint of the poor rather than as a literal, inerrant text, a stance the Vatican instruction criticised as selective.

gendered-self-government.rationale: The 1960s-80s Latin American strand rarely addressed gender in self-government; this is inferred from its general egalitarianism, and feminist strands are outside the scope.

defend-planned-state.rationale: Adherents were split: some sympathised with Cuba or Nicaragua while the movement as a whole did not endorse bureaucratic planned states; inferred from its use of Marxist analysis.

indirect-election.rationale: Inferred from the emphasis on grassroots base communities and popular participation, which points to direct rather than delegated choice.

national-church-status.rationale: Inferred from the movement's critique of the church's alliance with elites and Medellin's call to distance the church from power.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: Inferred from solidarity with oppressed and indigenous peoples; the movement did not address territorial autonomy directly.

disputed-territory-plebiscite.rationale: The movement did not address territorial disputes; no clear position can be inferred from its principles.

keep-colonial-borders.rationale: The movement did not address borders; no clear position can be inferred from its principles.

simple-living.rationale: Inferred from the movement's emphasis on evangelical poverty and solidarity with the poor.

restrict-indigenous-settlement.rationale: Inferred only from general solidarity with indigenous peoples; the movement did not address settlement restrictions specifically.

equal-conscription.rationale: Not addressed by the movement; its pacifist and just-war strands and its silence on gender make any inference weak.

homeland-spiritual-bond.rationale: Inferred: the movement rarely discusses national homeland as a spiritual matter; it focuses on the poor and structural injustice.

extrajudicial-killing.rationale: Romero denounced killings and violations of human rights, and the movement treats human life and legal protection as essential.

close-ties-china.rationale: Anachronistic: the movement's core texts do not address China; dependency theory opposes dependence on any great power.

protect-kin-minorities.rationale: Inferred: liberation theology was concerned with the poor within nations, and the sources do not address kin minorities abroad.

resources-common-ownership.rationale: The 1986 Vatican instruction recalls that property has a social purpose and the goods of the earth are meant for all, a view liberation theologians stress strongly.

self-ownership.rationale: Inferred: the movement stresses solidarity and the social dimension of property over individualist rights, though it affirms human dignity.

cut-consumption-tax.rationale: Inferred from the preferential option for the poor: consumption taxes fall hardest on the poor, but the sources do not discuss taxation.

targeted-social-spending.rationale: Inferred from the preferential option for the poor, though adherents also defend universal rights to basic goods, so the answer is not firm.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: Inferred: the movement builds from grassroots base communities and does not favour a leader above parties, but it does not discuss the question directly.

no-business-privileges.rationale: Inferred: structural sin and criticism of unjust economic structures imply opposition to privileges for powerful business interests.

no-denominational-politics.rationale: Adherents are split or silent: the movement is itself a religious force in politics, while the Church also asks clergy to avoid partisan roles.

tech-with-ancestral-values.rationale: Inferred: the movement does not address this tension; it respects popular religion but is oriented to historical liberation.

wife-divorce-without-consent.rationale: Inferred: the movement is Catholic and rarely addresses divorce, and adherents differ from the official Church line.

national-resource-control.rationale: Dependency analysis is central to the movement: poverty is explained by foreign economic domination, which favours national control of resources.

distribution-by-process.rationale: The preferential option for the poor judges structures by their effect on the poor, so an unequal outcome can be unjust whatever its process.

financial-transactions-tax.rationale: Inferred from the critique of structural injustice and global dependency; not addressed directly.

racism-not-main-obstacle.rationale: Inferred from its attention to the oppression of indigenous and Black Latin Americans as part of structural sin; not addressed as a general claim.

unjust-law-not-binding.rationale: Romero told soldiers that no one need obey an order against God's law, in line with the Catholic tradition behind the movement.

automate-paid-work.rationale: Not addressed directly; inferred from the concern that work serve human dignity and the poor.

multipolar-world.rationale: Inferred from its critique of dependency and imperial domination of Latin America; not stated as a world order.

labour-theory-of-value.rationale: The movement uses Marxist social analysis, but whether it endorses the labour theory of value itself is not stated in the sources.

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: Not addressed; adherents combine love of the people and nation with an international solidarity of the poor, and views vary.

material-over-identity.rationale: It centres the poor and class analysis but also stresses indigenous and cultural recognition, and adherents differ.

market-under-party-rule.rationale: Inferred: it draws on Marxist analysis but is committed to democratic base communities and the Church, and it is not a communist-party movement.

missingStatements.text: Laws and institutions should give first priority to the needs of the poor.
missingStatements.rationale: The preferential option for the poor is the movement's defining commitment and the Vatican also affirms it as an authentic evangelical concern.

notes: Adherents differ on violence (Câmara and Gutiérrez refuse to condemn the oppressed's violence; Romero rejected it) and on how far to use Marxism. Black, feminist, Dalit and Palestinian strands would answer several social and Israel questions differently.
